reviewer: Codex assistant; not independent human ground truth
method: Native goal-mouth contact sheets at5fps plus the earlier chronological whole-segment review. First New Jersey context answers were already known; this is a diagnostic review, not blinded evaluation. No count overrides were applied.

observations.note: Two distinct white attacking stick actions and two goalkeeper responses are consistent with a shot and rebound attempt. Ball-pad contacts remain difficult to resolve; retain the contextual label.
White attacks through the crease and celebrates. The later scoreboard change and center restart support a goal; exact finishing touch is occluded.
Red shooting stroke from the near side and subsequent keeper pad action. A small ball is visible on the initial path, but the final interception is not independently resolved.
The first red action could be a centering feed. A separate net-front sweep and keeper cover follow. Distinguishing an on-target shot from a pass collected by the goalie remains difficult.
Crowded faceoff and crease sequence. No clean ball-to-goal path established in the reviewed crops.
White long-range release followed by a camera pan and goalie response. The pan hides the trajectory; save versus miss is unresolved from these sheets.
Red rush followed by a shooting action and celebration. Later score change supports the goal. Camera crop clips part of the approach, so full-frame context matters.

White net drive produces a pad response and continued crease action, followed by celebration and later score change. Exact rebound count requires care; a later stick action alone is not proof of a second shot.
Green net-front play, referee pointing and celebration, with a later center restart in the raw sequence, support a goal. The crossing is obscured.
Light-gray attacking play reaches a crowded crease. Ball later appears toward the left side; the sampled sequence does not decisively distinguish a save from a wide path.
Orange net-front shooting action enters traffic. Contact is obscured; do not treat goalkeeper movement alone as a confirmed save.
Orange release from the wing and a later keeper response are visible. The small ball and final contact remain difficult to establish.
Light-gray net-front play is heavily screened. A loose ball emerges to the left, but an attacking release and the precise interception are not resolved.
Camera points down during much of the approach and release; the subsequent keeper response and ball near the crease do not independently establish an on-target save.
